title: Rewards
log: 2026-10-29T12:22:32Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: No point in the bank covers monetary and non-monetary rewards or performance pay; the behavioural and scientific approaches touch on motivation and pay for output but are different, broader ideas.

draft.title: Rewards
card: payments to staff, such as wages, salaries and bonuses. They give staff money they can spend.
benefits that are not cash, such as flexible hours, praise and recognition, or a chance to take on interesting work. They can meet needs that pay does not.
pay that is linked to results, such as a sales commission or a bonus for meeting a target. Staff who produce more can earn more.
Businesses often use both kinds of reward together. Rewards can motivate staff, but the effect depends on what each worker values.
draft.remember: Rewards can be money or not, and performance pay ties them to results.

a.q: Which of these is a non-monetary reward?
opts: Letting a worker start and finish early to suit family needs
Paying a worker a yearly bonus for reaching a target
Paying a worker a commission on each sale made
Raising a worker's salary after a yearly review
a.why: Flexible hours are a benefit that is not cash, so they are non-monetary. A bonus is tempting but it is a payment, so it is monetary, as are commission and a salary rise.
a.clue: Which reward is not a payment of money?

b.q: Priya runs a Newcastle solar panel business. She pays her sales team a set commission on each system sold. Which reward is this?
opts: Performance pay, because pay depends on sales results
Non-monetary, because it is not part of a regular wage
Non-monetary, because it is offered only to the sales team
Performance pay, because it is paid once a year as a bonus
b.why: The commission rises with the number of systems sold, so pay is linked to results. That makes it performance pay, which is also monetary. Being outside a regular wage does not make a reward non-monetary, because it is still money.
b.clue: What does the amount paid depend on?

a.best: Letting a worker start and finish early to suit family needs

b.best: Performance pay, because pay depends on sales results
